categories.label: Speech
categories.description: Human speech or conversation near the microphone. Broadband, non-periodic transients can trip an onset detector that keys on sudden energy, and a confidence-only classifier is not reliably lower on speech than on a real strum (ml/negatives.py root cause).

categories.label: Body/percussive tapping
categories.description: Finger or palm taps on the guitar body (not a strum across the strings). Shares the sharp, short-decay onset shape of a real strum onset.

categories.label: Desk/table knock
categories.description: A knuckle or object knock on the table or surface the guitar rests near. Produces a broadband transient similar in shape to a pick attack.

categories.label: Pick click
categories.description: The pick clicking against a string edge or the guitar body without a full strum across the strings. Carries the pick's characteristic high-frequency click without the harmonic content of a real chord strum.

categories.label: String noise
categories.description: String squeak or rattle produced by hand movement (repositioning, muting) rather than an intended strum. Overlaps in frequency content with a real down/up strum onset.

categories.label: Fret squeak
categories.description: The fretting hand sliding along a wound string between chord shapes. A short, high-pitched transient that can register as onset energy between confirmed chords.

categories.label: Metronome click
categories.description: An audible click-track or metronome tick playing in the room or through headphones bleed. Regular, sharp transients that can alias with onset detection at a steady tempo.

categories.label: Background music
categories.description: Recorded or streamed music playing in the room, not produced by the guitar being evaluated. Can carry real guitar-like onset and chord energy from another instrument.

categories.label: Television audio
categories.description: Television dialogue or soundtrack audio bleeding into the capture. Speech-like and music-like content mixed together, both hard-negative-relevant on their own.

categories.label: Fan/HVAC noise
categories.description: Continuous fan, air conditioner or other HVAC white noise. Mostly a false-negative risk for onset masking, but its edges (fan turning on/off) can register as spurious onsets.

categories.label: Phone handling
categories.description: Picking up, moving, or vibrating a phone near the microphone. A short, often broadband thump or buzz that resembles a percussive guitar-body tap.
